# Round 3 plan: triage

Round 3 keeps the same 40 tickets. It adds config E, which is C with the outage status check split back out. It parks D and runs 5 trials per cell. In round 2 the naive "same as last round" guess beat my prediction in 4 of 5 rows. So this round I move a number only when a failure ID gives the reason.

Defaults I chose:
- The round 2 section you pasted gives priority only for C and cost only for D. For the other cells I predict "no change from the r02 measured value". `r03.yaml` will store that r02 number, read from the r02 results.
- New requirement IDs start at R20. If R20 is already taken in `spe/spec/spec.md`, I will use the next free ID.

## Specify

### Proposals from round 2

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt as a new config E. C stays unchanged. | C stays as the control. E differs from C in one thing, so any change between them comes from the split. |
| P2 | Reject for r03. Logged as disagreement D1. | 0.86 is not a ceiling. That is about 5 of 40 tickets wrong, so there is room to improve. The 10 new tickets need reference labels from the support lead, and only the user can arrange that. Adding them now would also break comparison with r02 for every config. |
| P3 | Adopt as "park D for r03" (default). Logged as disagreement D2. | F6 has no fix yet. D also inherits F4 from C. Running D again would mostly repeat the same failure. D comes back as E on Haiku with a retry cap once F6 has a fix. |
| P4 | Adopt. | Reruns of the same 40 tickets give different answers, and 5 trials measure that spread better. One caveat: 5 trials do not shrink ticket-level noise. One ticket is worth 0.025, and B's 0.02 miss is smaller than one ticket. So bands widen to at least ±0.05, which is 2 tickets. |

## Predict

The baseline is r02 measured, regraded with the F5 fix. Each Why names the evidence for any move.

| Metric (grader check) | A | B | C | E | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy (`grade.py` category_match on `label.category`) | 0.86 ± 0.05 | 0.86 ± 0.05 | 0.80 ± 0.05 | 0.83 ± 0.05 | A, B, and C are unchanged. E moves up 0.03 because the status check helps separate outage from bug (F4). The move is small because naive won 4 of 5 rows in r02. |
| Priority accuracy (`grade.py` priority_match on `label.priority`) | r02 ± 0.05 | r02 ± 0.05 | 0.71 ± 0.05 | 0.77 ± 0.05 | A, B, and C are unchanged. C fell 0.07 (about 3 tickets) when its outage tickets got P3 (F4). E should recover most of that. |
| Status check call rate on outage tickets (trace check `tool_called(outage_status)`) | r02 ± 0.10 | r02 ± 0.10 | 0.00 + 0.10 | 0.95 ± 0.05 | F4 says C never called the check. E exposes the check as its own tool. |
| Cost per ticket (`grade.py` cost from logged usage tokens) | r02 ± 15% | r02 ± 15% | r02 ± 15% | C r03 + 5% ± 10% | A, B, and C are unchanged. E adds one tool definition and one extra call on outage tickets. |

One caveat on the 0.78 to 0.71 drop for C: it holds only if r01 was also regraded with the F5 fix. If r01 was not regraded, part of the drop may come from the grader. Gate 2 below checks this before E's priority number is final.

## Evaluate

### Gates, in order

1. **Grader selftest.** Run `grade.py` on its fixtures, including the R22 fixture. Every fixture must pass. Halt on any failure.
2. **Control regrade.** Regrade the r02 transcripts with the current `grade.py`. The result must reproduce the regraded r02 numbers exactly: category A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80, and priority C 0.71. I will also regrade r01 C priority to confirm the 0.78 baseline. Halt on any mismatch.
3. **Dry run.** Run 1 trial on 3 tickets for each of A, B, C, and E. T17 is one of the 3 tickets. Pass if:
   - E calls the status check on T17.
   - All R24 fields are filled.
   - The R25 hash matches.
   - No reference label appears in any prompt or tool output. A leaked label is an answer-key leak, and I halt.
4. **Launch the Workflow.**

### Workflow arguments

- Script: `spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js`
- Round: `r03`
- Configs: `A, B, C, E`
- Tickets: the r02 40-ticket set (hash checked)
- Trials: `5`
- Budget cap: `$25`. If the cap is reached, the run halts and I report.

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

- The run is 4 configs × 40 tickets × 5 trials = 800 agent runs, plus 12 dry-run runs. Round 2 was 480 runs.
- D on Haiku measured $0.004 per ticket. Sonnet costs several times more per token, so I estimate $0.006 to $0.015 per ticket for A, B, C, and E. That puts the total at about $5 to $12.
- I will replace this estimate with the r02 measured cost for A, B, and C before launch.

2. Append the r03 requirement table to `spe/spec/spec.md` and mark P1 to P4 resolved. Add D1 and D2 to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Commit locally with `spe r03: specify`.
3. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r03.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` from the Predict table with `status: final` and `supersedes: r03-draft.yaml`. Leave the draft file untouched. Commit locally with `spe r03: predict`.
4. Run gates 1 to 3, then launch the Workflow.
5. When the run ends, fill the round 3 section of `spe/prediction-log.md` and update `spe/failures.md` (close F4 if R21 passes). Commit locally with `spe r03: evaluate`.

All commits are local only. Nothing is pushed.

The stop rule needs 3 rounds in a row where predictions match results. Round 2 had 1 hit in 5 rows, so it does not apply yet.
